## Why this file exists

Every competitor/reference clone lives under `vendor/eval/`, which `.gitignore` excludes on purpose ("reference
clones … must never enter the tree's history"). So a review's **pinned HEAD, commit date and licence** are
evidence that exists only outside git: one worktree sweep, one re-clone, or one machine move and the review
cannot be reproduced or diffed. `docs/runbooks/competitor-review.md` names a missing HEAD as an anti-pattern
("Claims are not reproducible; a re-review cannot diff"), and on 2026-10-28 the pointer had to carry seven pins
as a hand-typed table labelled *"these pins live ONLY in this file"*. Hand-typed pins drift — and the drift is
invisible, because the thing they describe is not in git either.

This file is the tracked artifact. `--check` enforces the two properties that make it worth having: the table
matches the clones (HEAD, date, licence, tag), **and** the table is tracked (`git ls-files`). `--write` refuses a
gitignored target outright.

## What each column is, and what it is not

- **pinned HEAD / commit date** — `git -C vendor/eval/<name> rev-parse HEAD`, `log -1 --format=%cI`. Reproducible.
- **license** — read from the clone's own `LICENSE`/`COPYING` (the evidence path is in the cell), matched against
  a signature. Check it **before** borrowing: a copyleft or missing licence is an escalation to the operator, not
  a quiet copy.
- **shallow** — a `--depth 1` clone has **no tags** and no history, so a re-review must `git fetch --unshallow
  origin` **in place**; deleting the clone loses the pin.
- **latest remote tag** — the highest **version-like** tag on `origin`. Do not use `ls-remote --tags | tail -1`:
  that is ref order, and re-running it on 2026-10-28 put `nightly` in `symphony`'s tag cell and
  `test-simplify-docker-ci` in `openhands`'s — the same command `docs/SELFDEV.md` recommends.
- **manifest version** — printed because it is a **trap**, not as evidence: `openhands`' root `package.json` is
  the `@openhands/agent-canvas` sub-package, `hermes-agent`'s `pyproject.toml` says `0.0.0` while its
  `package.json` says `1.0.0`, and `oh-my-pi`'s has no version at all. Cite the tag and the commit date.
- **maturity** — a judgement the tool refuses to make (activity from the commit date, and whether the project
  ships its spec ahead of its code — `symphony`'s `SPEC.md` is "Draft v1"). Fill it in the review, by hand, with
  a path.

## Scope

Only `vendor/eval/*` git clones. **pi itself is pinned elsewhere and is not in this table**: `pi-main.pin.json`
(tracked: sha + package list) driven by `scripts/sync-pi.mjs` (`--sync` / `--link` / `--update`), because that
pin is a build input rather than review evidence. `vendor/pi-main/` and `vendor/pi-warden/` are built trees,
reproducible from their pins.

Per-project review headers (the `competitor-review.md` **Do 2** artifact) are emitted by
`node tools/vendor-pins.mjs --format header --project <name> --tags`. The review itself goes in
`docs/reviews/<name>-review.md`; the decision list is `docs/COMPETITORS.md`.

**How to read this table.** It is generated from the live clones; regenerate it with the command at the top of the file and never hand-edit between the markers.

`pinned HEAD` and `commit date` come from `git -C <clone> rev-parse HEAD` and `log -1 --format=%cI`; `license` is read out of the clone's own `LICENSE`/`COPYING` file (evidence path in the cell), never from a badge; `latest remote tag` is the highest **version-like** tag on `origin` via `git -C <clone> ls-remote --tags origin` — a bare `tail -1` is ref order, and picks labels like `nightly`.

`manifest version` is printed because it is a trap, not because it is evidence — cite the tag and the commit date. `maturity` is a judgement the tool refuses to make.
